```{r}

job = list(
  title   = "Research Data Scientist, Magic Eye",
  company = "Google",
  salary  = list(min = 147000, max = 210000)
)
str(job)


# Write one expression to extract each of
# 1. The company name.
job[[2]] #if you were to use one sq bracket, it would have returned a list

#or you can use
company_alt = job$company     #you are naming the company as company alt combining the job column and the vector within it so you can just pull that vector

# 2. The maximum salary.

maximum_salary = job$salary$max

# naming this value as maximum salary then you are pulling from the job list, the salary column, and then the maximum within the vector because it is two values

# 3. The maximum salary again, using only [[ ]].

max_salary_alt = job[[3]][[2]]   #in this you are pulling from job the third element (salary) then the second element within salary (max)

# 4. The names of the elements in job.
# Type them in a chunk in your markdown and run each line. The ad is the Google posting from Class 01.

names(job)




```


#subsetting and indexing
```{r}
crashes_by_day = c(2020, 2241, 2327, 2285, 2380, 1866, 1664)
names(crashes_by_day) = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu","Fri", "Sat", "Sun")

crashes_by_day[2]                      # one position

crashes_by_day[c("Wed", "Fri")] # Pulling elements by their name

crashes_by_day[] # returns all the elements


```
